query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a nanocrystalline TiN coating via physical vapor deposition (PVD) onto TC4 alloy surfaces will enhance hardness and wear resistance without significantly compromising the alloy’s beneficial mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified α + β dual-phase TC4 (Ti6Al4V) alloy.
generation.intervention: Deposition of a nanocrystalline TiN coating using a controlled PVD process.
generation.conditions: Testing under high-contact-stress, extreme service conditions (ambient to moderate temperatures, below the TiN thermal degradation threshold, e.g., <500°C).
generation.structural_mediator: A nanocrystalline TiN layer that forms a hard, adherent, and wear-resistant interface on the TC4 surface.
generation.mechanism: The TiN coating increases the surface hardness and serves as a barrier that reduces friction and wear through its inherent ceramic properties while the underlying TC4 maintains its original toughness and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated TC4, the TiN-coated TC4 is expected to exhibit a significantly higher surface hardness and lower wear rate under high-contact-stress conditions, while retaining similar bulk mechanical properties.
generation.baseline: Performance metrics (hardness, friction, wear resistance) of untreated TC4 under identical test conditions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is expected to hold under service temperatures up to about 500°C; beyond this, coating degradation may occur. Long-term cyclic loading could also potentially affect the coating’s adhesion, representing a limitation of the intervention.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty remains regarding the long-term adhesion and fatigue performance of the TiN coating in cyclic loading environments, as well as the precise improvement magnitude in wear resistance.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of TC4 alloy specimens: one set with the nanocrystalline TiN coating applied by PVD and one set left untreated. Subject both sets to identical high-contact-stress wear tests (e.g., pin-on-disc tests) at ambient to moderate temperatures. Conduct surface hardness measurements, quantify wear volume, and record friction coefficients after testing.
measurements: Wear volume (via profilometry or weight loss analysis)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the TiN-coated specimens do not show a statistically significant increase in surface hardness and a corresponding reduction in wear volume and friction coefficient compared to untreated TC4 specimens under the test conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.
